label: b8: lam95, seed 3 of 4 — wave 2 of 2
notes: Batch b8 -- what fixes b4's collapse. Everything is held at b4's config: fc (200,100), 8 epochs, b2's reward function, PPO's defaults elsewhere, seeds 1-4 pinned to the arm letters. One knob moves per group of four. **b4 itself is the control** -- 8 seeds at this exact config -- so no control arms are queued; compare against b4 TRUNCATED TO 100M, since 65% of its >=98%/500 rows land after 100M and the full-run figure is not the right comparator. The effect being tested: past its competence onset b4 spends a median 9.1% of its evals below 50% perfect, against 0.7% for b6 (same network, 4 epochs) and 0.0% for b5 (fc 320, 8 epochs), and its >=98%/500 density is the worst of the three at 7.3%. 100M rather than b4's 200M because the drawdown rate is already 8.5% in the first 100M and 9.0% in the second -- the effect is fully developed by this cap, though it is invisible at 10M. b3's two lambda arms had the best drawdown profile in the whole sweep -- 0.0% of post-competence evals below 50% AND below 80%, at a mean of 93.9 against the reference's 88.2 -- and lambda has never been tried at more than one seed. 0.95 is also the conventional PPO value; snek3 defaults to 0.98.
